chunks: 6 - He said: Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Umar al-Ji‘abi narrated to us, saying: Abu Abdillah Muhammad ibn al-Qasim al-Muharibi narrated to us, saying: Ismail ibn Ishaq al-Rashidi narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Harith narrated to us, saying: Ibrahim ibn Muhammad narrated to us, from Muslim al-A‘war, from Habbah al-‘Urani, from Abu al-Haytham ibn al-Tihan al-Ansari, who said:

The Messenger of God, peace be upon him and his family, said: Indeed God, Almighty and Glorious, created the souls two thousand years before the bodies and attached them to the Throne, and commanded them to greet me and obey me. And the first among men who greeted me and obeyed me was the soul of Ali ibn Abi Talib, peace be upon him.

key_terms.الْأَرْوَاحَ: The souls: the spiritual essences created by God before the physical bodies
key_terms.الْعَرْشِ: The Throne: the greatest of God's creations, symbolizing divine sovereignty
key_terms.بِالتَّسْلِيمِ: Greeting/salutation: an act of recognition and submission to prophetic authority

ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet say about the creation of souls and Ali's primacy?
ai.summary: This hadith conveys a prophetic tradition about the pre-creation of souls. The Prophet Muhammad (SAWW) declares that God created the souls two thousand years before the bodies and attached them to the Divine Throne. He then commanded them to greet and obey the Prophet. Among all men, the soul of Ali ibn Abi Talib (AS) was the first to greet and obey the Prophet. This teaching, reported by the companion Abu al-Haytham ibn al-Tihan al-Ansari during a gathering in Baghdad, establishes the primordial superiority of Imam Ali (AS) through divine pre-ordainment, serving as evidence for his wilayah (authority) among the Shia tradition.
